question: A 30-year-old woman presents with bilateral, symmetrical erythematous plaques on both shins for six weeks. She has a family history of psoriasis. The lesions have not improved despite one week of oral amoxicillin. Which feature MOST strongly suggests a non-infective (inflammatory) aetiology?

answers.text: Bilateral symmetrical distribution with failure to respond to antimicrobials

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Bilateral symmetrical distribution and failure to respond to antibiotics are strong indicators of a non-infective cause (inflammatory/autoimmune/allergic). Infections are typically unilateral, asymmetric, and respond to appropriate antimicrobials. Combined with family history of psoriasis, this pattern points toward an inflammatory dermatosis.

answers.text: Acute onset with localised heat, tenderness, and erythema

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Acute onset with localised heat, tenderness, and erythema are cardinal features of INFECTION (cellulitis/erysipelas). Non-infective dermatoses typically have a more insidious course, less tenderness, and lack the acute inflammatory triad.

Incorrect. Fever and draining lymphadenopathy suggest a systemic immune response to microbial invasion — strongly favouring an infective cause. Non-infective skin conditions (psoriasis, eczema) rarely cause febrile lymphadenopathy.

answers.text: History of recent skin trauma providing a portal of entry

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A documented skin breach (wound, abrasion, insect bite) provides a portal of entry for pathogens and strongly suggests infection (cellulitis, erysipelas). Non-infective inflammatory conditions lack an identifiable inoculation site.

overallFeedback.feedback: Infective features: unilateral, acute, hot, tender, fever, lymphadenopathy, portal of entry, antibiotic-responsive. Non-infective features: bilateral/symmetrical, chronic, antibiotic-resistant, steroid-responsive, family history of inflammatory disease.

Key non-infective indicators: bilateral/symmetrical, no fever, no response to antibiotics, positive family history for inflammatory disease, response to immunomodulators (steroids). This analytical framework helps avoid unnecessary antibiotic courses.
